weeks.weekly_summary: Establishing aerobic base with easy runs and one introductory quality session. Focus on consistent, conversational-pace running to build foundational fitness.
weeks.coaching_notes: No recent Strava data available; Week 1 establishes baseline at 7 hours/week. Three easy runs (Thu, Fri, Sun) + one moderate tempo introduction (Sat) + long run (Mon). Rest Wed, Tue to allow recovery between quality sessions. Pace conservatively—this is the foundation week.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 2 increases volume by ~8% with a second quality session (intervals). Long run grows to 14 km.

days.title: Easy 8km
days.description: Conversational pace easy run. Warm up with 1 km gentle jogging, run 6 km steady easy, cool down 1 km.
days.notes: Start the block conservatively. Focus on relaxed breathing and form.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day. Allow the body to adapt to the training stimulus.

days.title: Tempo Introduction 10km (6 min @ easy, 4 min tempo, 6 min easy, 4 min tempo, 6 min easy)
days.description: Warm-up 2 km easy. Then: 4 min at tempo pace (comfortably hard), 2 min easy recovery. Repeat 4 min tempo, 2 min easy. Cool down 2 km easy. This is a fartlek-style introduction to lactate threshold work.
days.notes: Keep tempo segments controlled; this is an introduction, not a full 10 km effort.

days.title: Easy 7km
days.description: Relaxed, conversational-pace easy run. 1 km warm-up, 5 km steady easy, 1 km cool-down.
days.notes: Keep HR low; this is active recovery from Saturday's tempo work.

days.title: Long Run 12km Easy
days.description: Sustained easy-pace long run. Warm up 1 km, run 10 km at easy conversational pace, cool down 1 km. Focus on steady effort and breathing.
days.notes: This establishes the long-run baseline. Run with consistency, not speed.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day. Recovery is essential after the long run.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day. Prepare for Week 2 buildup.

weeks.weekly_summary: Volume increases ~8% to 45.5 km. Two quality sessions (tempo + interval repeats) integrated with easy runs. Long run grows to 14 km. Maintaining 80/20 polarization.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 2 introduces interval repeats (VO2 max stimulus) on Thursday. Saturday tempo run builds on Week 1 foundation. Long run progresses to 14 km (+2 km). Three easy runs + two quality sessions across the week, with rest days strategically placed.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 3 peaks with 10% increase to 50 km total. Long run reaches 16 km. Two quality sessions maintain threshold and VO2 max stimulus.

days.title: VO2 Max Intervals 10km (6 × 800m @ 4:00/km, 90s jog recovery)
days.description: Warm up 2 km easy. Then 6 × 800m repeats at VO2 max pace (approximately 3:55–4:05/km), with 90 seconds easy jogging recovery between repeats. Cool down 1 km easy.
days.notes: Keep 90s recovery active; don't stop completely. Maintain form on final reps.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day. Recovery after hard interval session.

days.title: Sustained Tempo 10km @ Tempo Pace
days.description: Warm up 2 km easy. Run 6 km steady at tempo pace (comfortably hard, ~5:10/km pace equivalent for a competitive runner). Cool down 2 km easy.
days.notes: Sustain effort without going anaerobic. Should be able to speak in short sentences.

days.title: Easy 8km
days.description: Easy-pace recovery run. 1 km warm-up, 6 km steady easy, 1 km cool-down.
days.notes: Active recovery from Saturday's tempo work. Keep conversational.

days.title: Long Run 14km Easy
days.description: Sustained easy-pace long run. 1 km warm-up, 12 km at easy conversational pace, 1 km cool-down. Build time on feet.
days.notes: Pace grows by 2 km. Focus on steady effort; practice fueling strategy if applicable.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day. Prepare for Week 3 peak training.

weeks.weekly_summary: Peak training week (+10% to 50 km total). Two quality sessions maintained (interval repeats + tempo). Long run reaches 16 km. Cumulative volume highest before Week 4 recovery.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 3 is the cumulative peak of this block. Interval repeats on Thursday target VO2 max; tempo on Saturday builds lactate threshold. Long run reaches 16 km (+2 km from Week 2). Three easy runs provide aerobic base. No two hard sessions on consecutive days; hard sessions separated from long run.
weeks.next_week_preview: Week 4 is recovery week: reduce volume by 20% to ~40 km. Keep one quality session (tempo) but shorten long run to 13 km. Prepare body for next training block.

days.title: VO2 Max Intervals 11km (8 × 800m @ 4:00/km, 90s jog recovery)
days.description: Warm up 2 km easy. Then 8 × 800m repeats at VO2 max pace (~3:55–4:05/km), with 90 seconds easy jogging between repeats. Cool down 1 km easy.
days.notes: Two additional reps vs Week 2. Maintain consistent pace across all reps. Form focus on final reps.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day.

days.title: Sustained Tempo 11km (8 km @ Tempo Pace)
days.description: Warm up 2 km easy. Run 8 km steady at tempo pace (comfortably hard, ~5:10/km equivalent). Cool down 1 km easy.
days.notes: Extended from 6 km to 8 km. Sustain effort; this is a cornerstone session.

days.title: Easy 9km
days.description: Easy-pace recovery run. 1 km warm-up, 7 km steady easy, 1 km cool-down.
days.notes: Active recovery. Keep conversational throughout.

days.title: Long Run 16km Easy
days.description: Sustained easy-pace long run. 1 km warm-up, 14 km at easy conversational pace, 1 km cool-down. Build time on feet toward marathon distance.
days.notes: Peak long run of this block (+2 km from Week 2). Practice your race-day fueling and hydration strategy.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day. Prepare for Week 4 recovery block.

weeks.weekly_summary: Recovery week: volume reduced 20% to ~40 km. One quality session (tempo) maintained to preserve fitness. Long run shortened to 13 km. Focus on recovery and consolidation before next training block.
weeks.coaching_notes: Week 4 is a strategic recovery week per periodization rules. Total volume drops by ~20% vs Week 3 (50 → 40 km). One quality session (tempo on Saturday) maintains stimulus without excessive fatigue. Long run reduces by 20% (16 → 13 km). Three easy runs + one tempo + recovery. This week allows adaptation and prepares the body for the next 4-week block's increased demands.
weeks.next_week_preview: After Week 4 recovery, the next 4-week block (Weeks 5–8) will focus on Aerobic Development with progressive long runs and tempo work, building toward Peak Training phases.

days.notes: Keep effort very conversational. This is recovery week.

days.description: Warm up 2 km easy. Run 5 km steady at tempo pace (comfortably hard). Cool down 2 km easy.
days.notes: Reduced volume (5 km tempo vs 8 km last week). Maintains stimulus without excessive fatigue in recovery week.

days.description: Easy-pace recovery run. 1 km warm-up, 6 km steady easy, 1 km cool-down.
days.notes: Active recovery from Saturday. Keep conversational throughout.

days.title: Long Run 13km Easy
days.description: Sustained easy-pace long run. 1 km warm-up, 11 km at easy conversational pace, 1 km cool-down.
days.notes: Reduced 20% from Week 3's 16 km (recovery week protocol). Maintains long-run stimulus at reduced intensity.

days.title: Rest / Recovery
days.description: Full rest day.

days.description: Full rest day. End of 4-week block. Recovery complete.
days.notes: Reassess fitness level and plan next training block. Consider any fatigue signals or adaptations needed.

roadmap.weekly_summary: Launch into Aerobic Development phase. Volume increases 30% from Week 4 recovery to 52 km. Long run builds to 18 km. Two quality sessions (tempo + intervals) establish lactate threshold and VO2 max. Focus on sustaining aerobic capacity while building marathon-specific endurance.

Aerobic Development continues. Volume grows modestly to 55 km (+6% from Week 5). Long run extends to 19 km. Quality sessions progress: tempo increases to 9 km; VO2 max work becomes longer repeats (1.2 km). Three easy runs maintain 80/20 polarization. Building aerobic engine for Peak Training.

Peak of Aerobic Development. Volume reaches 58 km (+5% from Week 6). Long run climbs to 20 km. Tempo extends to 10 km sustained effort. VO2 max work shifts to longer 1.5 km repeats. This week builds the aerobic foundation before transition to Peak Training with marathon-pace segments.

Recovery week at end of Aerobic Development block. Volume reduced 20% to 46 km. Long run shortened to 16 km. One quality tempo session (7 km) maintains fitness. Two easy runs plus recovery. Consolidates aerobic gains before Peak Training block (Weeks 9–12) introduces marathon-pace segments and increased intensity.

coaching_overview: This 4-week Base Building block establishes aerobic foundation with two quality sessions per week, progressive long runs (12 → 14 → 16 → 13 km), and 80/20 polarized training. Week 1 introduces tempo work at moderate intensity. Weeks 2–3 build with interval repeats (VO2 max) and sustained tempo, reaching peak volume of 50 km in Week 3. Week 4 is a strategic recovery week (40 km, reduced volume) to consolidate adaptations. Training respects 7-hour weekly time budget and applies periodization principles: no two hard sessions on consecutive days, hard sessions separated from long run, 10% weekly volume progression limit, and recovery week protocol. After Week 4, the Roadmap outlines Weeks 5–8 (Aerobic Development phase) with progressive long runs to 20 km and increased tempo/interval stimulus. Subsequent blocks will introduce Peak Training (Weeks 9–12) with marathon-pace segments and VO2 max work, followed by Taper and Race Week as the athlete approaches their marathon goal.
